title.narrative: Strengthening partnership between Shifting the Power consortium members INGOs and LNGOs (Output 3)

description.narrative:
The output 3 of shifting the power project focused on the fact that Shifting the Power consortium INGO members must recognise and respond to national organisations' voice and agency. Recognition has been growing within the wider humanitarian sector of the importance of local and national disaster management capacity. However much greater investment is required to develop and reinforce permanent local capacity to prepare for and respond to emergencies. As highlighted in the DEPP Business Case, in 2010 the Global Humanitarian Platform spoke of the need for a fundamental shift in approach to place national organisations at the centre of humanitarian action. The Missed Opportunities report highlights that “a strategic shift towards southern actors is not a neutral one, but will potentially see northern/western agencies lose out in terms of resources. Therefore any suggestion of a more localised approach to response is likely to be met with resistance, even if the humanitarian imperatives are clear-cut”.
The project will work with organisations to understand national organisations perspectives on humanitarian practice and barriers and challenges posed by international humanitarian agencies, providing space for self-reflection of International START Network agencies, and encouraging changes in practices and policies of international actors to support new roles and ways of working.
